text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] spike in 401s from edge-proxy -> api.redwood.ai (detected by rate-anomaly detector). initial sample: 2026-03-15T10:12Z. Suspected automated auth probe. tagging #incidents for triage.

oncall-sre: acked, I'm on it. forwarding to security for verification.
alex.sre: seeing a ~15x increase in 401/sec for /v1/generate from 10.12Z to 10.16Z, source IPs concentrated in two /20 blocks, sudden burst pattern.
maria.security: joining. any known deploys or config changes?
jen.prod: no deploys in that window, release freeze. Customer-impact?
alex.sre: so far upstream 401s only, no 5xxs. A handful of customers reported auth errors via support ticket, but looks like failed token use rather than service outage.
sam.infra: pulling logs + quick search for token reuse. I see repeated attempts with header Authorization: Bearer <bearer-like-string> from many IPs. Some tokens look like service tokens issued to an internal worker queue.
maria.security: oof. If internal service tokens are being probed, we need immediate containment and key rotation plan. Can we confirm tokens are valid and where they originated?
alex.sre: correlating token IDs to issuance: two token IDs map to svc:ingest-worker and svc:legacy-proxy. Timestamps show tokens issued 6 months ago and last used 2 hours before the spike.
incident-bot: action required: escalate to P1 if confirmed token compromise.
oncall-sre: setting incident severity to SEV2 for now until we confirm compromise. maria, can you take lead for token rotation? i'll own traffic blocking and customer comms.
maria.security: taking lead. immediate tasks: 1) block offending CIDR ranges at edge, 2) revoke suspect service tokens, 3) rotational key issuance and deploy, 4) validate no secrets leaked to external storage.
jen.prod: for customer-facing comms, please confirm which customers saw 401s (cs-lead listed).
cs-lead: pulling list from support. preliminary: 4 customers reported intermittent authentication failures between 10:12-10:20Z. no full outages; most recovered after retries.
sam.infra: applying temporary ipblock ACL on edge layer:
```
# allowlist-based deny for suspicious prefixes
edgectl acl add-deny --prefix 198.51.100.0/22 --reason "suspicious probe"
edgectl acl add-deny --prefix 203.0.113.0/22 --reason "suspicious probe"
```
edge responded: acl applied successfully at 10:22Z. observing immediate drop in new probe connections from those CIDRs.
alex.sre: good, 401 rate dropping to ~2x baseline after ACL. still seeing token usage from internal IPs though (possible replay via compromised host).
maria.security: revoking the two suspect service tokens now. Commands (internal):
```
redwoodctl auth revoke --token-id svc-ingest-202507 --force
redwoodctl auth revoke --token-id svc-legacy-202201 --force
```
redwoodctl responded: revoke accepted, tokens invalidated at 10:24Z.
alex.sre: confirm: requests that used those tokens now return 401 with "invalid_token" and are not accepted by the runtime. Verified by replaying a saved request - got 401.
maria.security: start issuing new tokens on rotated credentials. We will create new service principals with short TTL and rotate config for ingest-worker and legacy-proxy. jen, coordinate deploy windows.
jen.prod: can we do hot-rotate (rolling restart) of services to pick up new creds? we should avoid customer impact.
sam.infra: ingest-worker uses k8s secret mounted; plan: create new secret, update Deployment to use new secret via env var bump; rolling update will replace pods. estimated ~2-3min per pod, canary to 1 pod.
jen.prod: do canary to one zone first. schedule at 10:35Z.
cs-lead: telling affected customers: "We observed elevated authentication failures affecting a small number of API calls between 10:12-10:20Z. We implemented mitigations; no data access was observed. We'll follow up with timeline and next steps."
maria.security: quick artifact search: scanning S3 + internal CI logs for accidental leakage of service token strings. running query for the token prefixes and hashes. so far no matches in public buckets.
alex.sre: found interesting log excerpt in an internal debug bucket with truncated token-like strings (redacted here):
```
[2026-03-15T10:10:34Z] proxy-auth: failed auth attempt for token=***abcXYZ123 (len 32) src=198.51.100.12
[2026-03-15T10:11:01Z] proxy-auth: attempt token=***abcXYZ123 user=svc:ingest-worker src=198.51.100.50
```
maria.security: that suggests tokens were seen in logs and then replayed. immediate follow-up: audit who had access to that bucket and remove public READ perms.
sam.infra: I audited the S3 ACLs: the debug bucket had an accidental put ACL grant to a CI role that is external. removing grant and adding explicit deny for public at 10:28Z.
jen.prod: after revocation and ACL + rotate, can we confirm customer impact is resolved? alex?
alex.sre: 401 spike back to baseline and tickets show no new reports after 10:30Z. most retries succeed.
incident-bot: record action items: [block CIDRs] [revoked tokens] [rotated credentials] [removed ACL grant] [canary rotate services].
maria.security: next steps: 1) run full secret scan across artifacts and logs for last 90 days; 2) rotate any long-lived service tokens and enforce TTL <= 30d for service principals; 3) postmortem and access review for the debug bucket. I'll own 1+2.
oncall-sre: handing off to followup owners. tagging #postmortem and #sec-notify.
cs-lead: scheduling customer follow-up email with timeline + mitigations.
jen.prod: small note: legacy-proxy uses a fallback token store in Redis; if any rotated tokens were cached there, we need to flush. sam, can you flush cached tokens cluster-wide?
sam.infra: flushing token cache: `redis-cli -h tokens-redis -n 1 EVAL "return redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0` - will do after canary completes. doing at 10:38Z.
alex.sre: post-rotate checks: auth latency normal, downstream unaffected. assigning incident to postmortem queue.
maria.security: marking timeline and evidence in pagerduty ticket PD-987654 and starting secret-scan job.
cs-lead: final: no customer data exfil observed in initial checks, but we're keeping incident open until full secret-scan completes. ETA 24h for initial scan.
oncall-sre: closing real-time triage, switching to async. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
